term.value: OPERATIVE LEASE is the Amended and Restated Lease dated 2/25/2015, which RELOCATED OfficeMax/Office Depot from the original ~30,000 SF box to a new 16,724 SF space — so the tenant has been at 16,724 SF since 2015 (the 1996 OfficeMax lease is fully superseded). The A&R Lease had a 10-year Initial Term (≈10/1/2015–9/30/2025) plus two 5-year options ($24.20 then $26.62/SF). Tenant gave a Non-Renewal Notice (3/14/2025) declining the options, so the lease was set to expire 9/30/2025; KPR then signed a 2025 First Amendment extending ONE year to 9/30/2026 at a below-option $19.50/SF. During this extension EITHER party may terminate on 120–150 days' notice, and KPR has access to market/tour the space — i.e., this is a true short-term, exit-track occupancy.

exclusives.description: Tenant operates an office/consumer-supply store; the A&R Lease's Permitted Use is ANY lawful retail purpose (or no use), subject to the Center's Restricted Uses (Schedule E-1). coTenancy.value: Ongoing Co-Tenancy (A&R Lease §2.6): King Soopers (or a Qualified Replacement) PLUS at least one additional 15,000+ SF retailer must be open and operating (≥80% of their premises). If not met (beyond 180-day remodel/casualty closures), Tenant may pay 50% Reduced Rent for up to 24 months and, failing cure within a further 12 months, terminate on 60 days' notice. No Opening Co-Tenancy. Currently satisfied (King Soopers + Marshalls/Michaels/PetSmart operating).

camTax.value: Tenant pays its pro-rata share of Shared Charges (CAM, taxes, insurance). For pro-rata calculations, the Center Leasable Area has a 'Denominator Floor' of 220,000 SF (i.e., Tenant's share is never computed on less than 220,000 SF). Detailed CAM caps/exclusions per the A&R Lease (not fully extracted this pass).

flags.issue: Office Depot is on an EXIT track — non-renewed, now on a 1-year terminable extension (KPR marketing the space)
flags.detail: The operative lease is the 2/25/2015 Amended & Restated Lease (16,724 SF). Office Depot DECLINED its renewal options (Non-Renewal Notice 3/14/2025) and is occupying only under a 1-year KPR extension to 9/30/2026 at $19.50/SF, which EITHER party can end on 120–150 days' notice. KPR has the right to tour/market the space. Underwrite this as a near-term vacancy/re-tenanting opportunity (16,724 SF), not as in-place term. Note the 2025 First Amendment requires KPR to keep the termination/closing confidential from Office Depot store staff.

flags.issue: Bears directly on Michaels' co-tenancy — the OfficeMax/Office Depot anchor leg is leaving
flags.detail: Office Depot (the OfficeMax leg of Michaels' 3-anchor co-tenancy) is on an exit track (≤9/30/2026, possibly sooner). When it goes, Michaels falls to 2 of 3 (King Soopers + PetSmart) with no cushion — see the Michaels co-tenancy flag. A replacement for this 16,724 SF space that qualifies as an 'Anchor Tenant' under Michaels' lease (≥20 stores nationally / ≥7 regionally, or up to 2 tenants ≥21,000 SF / 70% of the OfficeMax space) would restore the cushion.

narrative: Office Depot (OfficeMax North America, Inc., an Ohio corporation; The ODP Corporation; store OMX #3362) occupies 16,724 SF at 2730 S Colorado Blvd in University Hills, Denver. The operative lease is the Amended & Restated Lease dated 2/25/2015, which relocated OfficeMax from the original ~30,000 SF box to this smaller 16,724 SF space — so the tenant has been at 16,724 SF since 2015 (the 1996 lease is fully superseded). The A&R Lease ran a 10-year term (~2015–2025) at $21.00→$22.00/SF with two 5-year options ($24.20, $26.62). Office Depot DECLINED renewal (Non-Renewal Notice 3/14/2025), so the lease was set to expire 9/30/2025; KPR then signed a First Amendment (7/23/2025) extending one year to 9/30/2026 at a below-option $19.50/SF ($326,118), with EITHER party able to terminate on 120–150 days' notice and KPR marketing the space. This is an exit-track, near-term vacancy — underwrite the 16,724 SF as a re-tenanting opportunity. It also matters for Michaels' co-tenancy: this OfficeMax leg is departing, dropping Michaels to 2 of 3 anchors. (This abstract corrects an earlier draft mistakenly built on the superseded 1996 OfficeMax lease.)
